newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 31.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Chung Tae-soo, founder of the Hanbo Group, was questioned by prosecutors throughout the night on how the conglomerate secured about five trillion won in loans.
- Seven South Korean nuclear activists were expelled by Taiwan after being beaten by right-wing Taiwanese groups. The leader of the group and two others were injured.
- Hanbo Group officials told state prosecutors the conglomerate had provided political funds to members of ruling and opposition parties, according to a senior official from the ruling camp.
- South Korea's economy continues to show signs of slowing. The unemployment rate is the highest since 1994 while consumer spending is the lowest in four years.
- The government has decided to help Hanbo Steel Co resume normal operation within three months. It will provide emergency funds.
